title: PartSpecV4_4
description: Part Spec v4.4 (v4.3 plus divided-scroll turbo housings: a volute can have 2 or 4 channels, each with its own inlet, and a set inlet diameter). 'draft' leans faces of a solid away from a neutral plane, as a moulded or cast part needs. Booleans, fillets, patterns, hollow, mirror and the other CAD features can name any plate, body, tube, reducer, volute or merge by id as a solid; one they use up is no longer part of the result. Everything from v4.3 still works. All lengths are in millimeters and all angles in degrees.

id.description: Unique feature id within the spec, referenced by other features.

point_mm.description: A point [x, y] in millimeters. In a plate or extrude outline it is in the plate's local frame, origin at the center. In a revolve profile it is [radius, z] from the axis and the base.

placement.description: Where a feature sits. 'anchor' is an anchor id picked on the scan, or 'origin' for the part's own local origin. Offsets are relative to that anchor, never absolute. Rotation is about the anchor's normal or axis.

counterbore.description: A through hole with a flat-bottomed recess on the top face, for a bolt head.

countersink.description: A through hole with a conical recess on the top face, for a flat-head screw.

slot.description: A through slot with rounded ends. length_mm is end to end.

standoff.description: A round post standing on a plate face. A positive hole_diameter_mm drills it through the post and the plate.

rib.description: A thin wall standing on a plate face along a line. 'rectangular' is a rib of constant height. 'triangular' is a gusset whose height falls from height_mm at start_mm to zero at end_mm.

bend.description: Joins an edge of one plate to an edge of another through a rounded bend, making an L or other angled bracket. The second plate's own placement is ignored; the bend positions it.

fillet.description: Rounds edges of a plate. 'vertical' is the outline corners, 'top' and 'bottom' are the face outlines, 'all' is every edge.

chamfer.description: Bevels edges of a plate. Edge selection is the same as for fillet.

cutout.description: A through cut around a clearance zone on the scan, such as a bolt head or a hose, positioned by an anchor. margin_mm grows the cut beyond the zone shape.

emboss_text.description: Text raised from, or engraved into, a plate face. height_mm is the letter height; depth_mm is how far it rises or sinks.

oneOf.description: A round plate centered on the plate origin. The edge is a true circle.
A closed polygon. The last point connects back to the first.

body.description: A solid with a height, for boxes, vases, cups and knobs. The body frame has its origin at the center of the base, Z up, so the base sits at Z = 0 and the top at Z = height_mm. 'shape' says how it is made; 'shell' hollows it; 'edge_fillet_mm' rounds the outer top and bottom edges, or use edge_fillet_top_mm and edge_fillet_bottom_mm to round them separately; 'bores' drills blind holes; 'texture' adds vertical ridges or grooves on the outside wall.

edge_fillet_mm.description: Radius that rounds the outer top and bottom edges. Must be smaller than the wall thickness when the body is hollow.

edge_fillet_top_mm.description: Radius that rounds only the outer top edge. Cannot be combined with edge_fillet_mm.

edge_fillet_bottom_mm.description: Radius that rounds only the outer bottom edge. Cannot be combined with edge_fillet_mm.

bores.description: Blind holes drilled into the body, such as the socket of a shift knob.

extrude.description: A prism: the outline, straight up by height_mm. A rectangle outline gives a box; a circle gives a cylinder.

shell.description: Hollows the body, leaving walls of wall_thickness_mm. open 'top' removes the top face (a vase, cup or box); 'none' makes a closed hollow part. The base stays as thick as the walls.

revolve.description: A solid of revolution about the body's Z axis: vases, cups, knobs, bottles. 'profile_mm' lists [radius, z] points of the outside surface from the base up to the rim, with z strictly increasing (no overhangs, so it prints without supports). The base is a flat disc from the axis out to the first point, and the top is closed flat unless the body is hollowed open at the top. Use many points for a smooth curve.

texture.description: A repeating pattern of vertical stripes on the outside wall: 'ridges' stand out by depth_mm, 'grooves' are cut in by depth_mm (and must be shallower than the wall if the body is hollow). 'spacing_mm' is the distance between stripe centers along a flat side, or around the widest part of a round body. Stripes run the full height unless 'z_range_mm' [from, to] limits them. Supported on rectangle and circle extrusions and on revolved bodies.

bore.description: A round hole drilled into a body along its Z axis and stopping at depth_mm (a blind bore). from 'bottom' drills up from the base face and 'top' drills down from the top face. position_mm is [x, y] from the body's center, default [0, 0]. For a threaded hole, use the tap-drill diameter (8.8 mm for M10x1.25), not the thread's outer diameter.

tube.description: A round pipe swept along a 3D path. 'path_mm' lists [x, y, z] corner points in the part frame (relative to 'placement'); each corner between two straight runs is rounded with 'bend_radius_mm' (the centerline radius, default 1.5 times the outer diameter). 'wall_thickness_mm' makes it hollow with open ends; leave it out for a solid rod. The ends are cut square to the first and last run.

merge.description: Fuses two or more tubes that overlap into one solid, then clears every tube's bore so the passages join (a collector where runners meet). The merged tubes are not built separately. A tube can be in only one merge.

reducer.description: A straight pipe whose outer diameter changes linearly from 'start_diameter_mm' at 'start_mm' to 'end_diameter_mm' at 'end_mm' (points in the part frame, relative to 'placement'). 'wall_thickness_mm' makes it hollow with open ends. It can join a merge like a tube.

flange.description: A bolted end plate on one end of a hollow tube or reducer ('tube' is its id, 'end' is 'start' or 'end' of the path). The flange face is flush with the pipe's open end and the plate extends back along the pipe by 'thickness_mm'. The pipe bore runs through it. Bolt holes are placed in the flange frame: origin on the pipe axis, X and Y in the face seen from outside, X chosen as the world Z axis crossed with the outward direction (world X if the pipe points along Z). On a volute the ends are 'inlet' (the straight inlet stub) and 'outlet' (the axial exhaust outlet); a volute with 2 or 4 channels has 'inlet_1' to 'inlet_N' instead of 'inlet'.

volute.description: A turbine-style scroll housing (turbo exhaust housing). Frame: origin on the wheel axis at the wheel plane, Z along the axis, outlet towards -Z. The passage starts at the tongue on the +X axis and winds counter-clockwise seen from +Z; its round section area grows linearly with angle and is sized so the largest section has the given 'a_over_r_cm' (area in cm2 over centroid radius in cm, as vendors quote A/R). Its inner edge opens onto the wheel cavity (inducer diameter plus clearance). The inlet is a straight stub of the largest section on the +X side, centered at x = cavity radius + largest section radius, flowing +Y and entering from -Y. The outlet is a cone down to the exducer bore. Walls are 'wall_thickness_mm' all round. Simplified: no wastegate, bearing flange or vanes. Part Spec 4.4: 'channels' (1, 2 or 4) divides the scroll into that many equal sectors of the circle, as a divided or four-port housing has. Channel i starts at its own tongue at angle (i-1)*360/N and winds counter-clockwise to angle i*360/N, where its own tangential inlet stub is (flowing counter-clockwise, entering from behind, at that angle). Each channel carries 1/N of the flow, so the A/R of each channel is 'a_over_r_cm' divided by N. Ends: 'inlet_1' to 'inlet_N' (for 1 channel just 'inlet') and 'outlet'. 'inlet_diameter_mm' (inner diameter) sets the open end of each inlet stub, which then narrows along 'inlet_length_mm' to the passage, so a real flange size can be used instead of the one derived from A/R. Simplified: the walls between channels are only as thick as the tongue gap, there is no flow simulation, wastegate or vanes.

sketch_loop.description: A closed 2D outline in the sketch plane (x, y in mm). 'circle', 'rectangle' (width along x) and 'ellipse' are centered on 'center_mm' (default [0, 0]). 'polygon' joins its points with straight lines. 'path' starts at 'start_mm' and follows 'segments': a 'line' to a point, a three-point 'arc' (through 'mid_mm' to 'to_mm') or a smooth 'spline' through the listed points (the last one is where it ends). A path closes itself back to its start with a straight line.

sketch.description: 2D shapes on a plane. 'plane' is 'XY' (x right, y up the sketch, normal +Z), 'XZ' (x = world X, y = world Z, normal -Y) or 'YZ' (x = world Y, y = world Z, normal +X), moved 'offset_mm' along its normal and/or to 'origin_mm' in the part frame. Each shape is an 'outer' outline with optional 'holes' (outlines inside it).

extrude_feature.description: Pushes a sketch into a solid. 'distance_mm' is the length; 'direction' is 'normal' (along the plane normal, default), 'reverse' or 'symmetric' (half each way); 'taper_deg' leans the sides in (positive) or out. 'operation' 'new' (default) makes a solid named by this feature's id; 'add', 'cut' and 'intersect' combine the result with the solid named by 'target', and the combined solid takes this feature's id.

revolve_feature.description: Spins a sketch about an axis in the sketch plane into a solid. 'axis' is a line from 'from_mm' to 'to_mm' in sketch coordinates (default: the sketch's y axis); the sketch must stay on one side of it. 'angle_deg' is the sweep (default 360). 'operation' and 'target' work as for extrude.

boolean.description: Combines solids: 'union' joins 'target' and every tool, 'cut' removes the tools from the target, 'intersect' keeps only the shared volume. The target and tools are used up; the result takes this feature's id.

transform.description: Moves a solid. Steps run in this order: 'mirror' across a plane ('XY', 'XZ' or 'YZ' of the part frame, moved 'offset_mm' along its normal), then 'rotate' about an axis through 'axis_point_mm' with direction 'axis_dir', then 'translate_mm'. The result takes this feature's id. With 'copy' true the source solid stays too (use it to repeat a shape); otherwise the source is used up.

curve.description: An open path on a plane (same planes as a sketch), for 'sweep' to follow. Starts at 'start_mm' and continues through line, 3-point arc and spline segments.

sweep.description: Drags the first outline of sketch 'profile' along curve 'path' to make a solid. The profile's plane should pass through the curve's start and face along it. 'operation' and 'target' work as for extrude.

loft.description: Blends a solid through two or more sketches in the order listed (each sketch holds one outline, no holes). 'ruled' joins them with straight faces instead of a smooth blend. 'operation' and 'target' work as for extrude.

edge_selector.description: Which edges. 'all', or a list of choices whose edges are combined: {parallel: X|Y|Z} straight edges running along that axis; {on_face: top|bottom|left|right|front|back} edges of the outermost face on that side (top +Z, bottom -Z, right +X, left -X, back +Y, front -Y); {near_mm: [x,y,z], within_mm: r} edges whose middle lies within r of the point.

fillet_edges.description: Rounds chosen edges of the solid named 'solid'. The solid is used up; the result takes this feature's id.

chamfer_edges.description: Bevels chosen edges of the solid named 'solid'. The solid is used up; the result takes this feature's id.

hollow.description: Makes the solid 'solid' thin-walled with wall 'thickness_mm', growing inward. 'open_sides' removes those sides (top +Z, bottom -Z, right +X, left -X, back +Y, front -Y) so the part becomes a cup or tray; with none, it is a closed hollow. The solid is used up; the result takes this feature's id.

linear_pattern.description: Repeats the solid 'source' 'count' times, each copy 'spacing_mm' [x,y,z] further along than the last, and joins them into one solid (copies must touch or be tools for a cut). The source is used up; the result takes this feature's id.

circular_pattern.description: Repeats the solid 'source' 'count' times around an axis through 'axis_point_mm' along 'axis_dir', spread over 'angle_deg' (default 360, evenly around; a smaller angle puts the first and last copies that far apart). Copies are joined into one solid.

mirror.description: Adds a mirrored copy of 'source' across plane 'plane' ('XY', 'XZ' or 'YZ', moved 'offset_mm'), joined to the original. The source is used up; the result takes this feature's id. (To keep them as two separate solids use 'transform' with mirror and copy.)

draft.description: Leans faces of 'solid' by 'angle_deg' (0.1 to 30), as a mould needs so the part can be pulled out. The neutral plane is at the bottom of the part along 'pull_direction' ('X', 'Y' or 'Z', default 'Z'), or at the top with neutral 'top'; faces stay put there and lean inward as they get further away (a positive angle makes the part narrower away from the neutral plane). 'faces' is 'sides' (every face except flat ones facing along the pull direction) or a list of sides (top, bottom, left, right, front, back) naming the outermost face on that side. The solid is used up; the result takes this feature's id.
